title: A Uniform for the Compass
premise: Jude Ashgrove, a courier for the collapsing Republic of Vessany, has survived by carrying sealed orders and asking no questions. When a stranger named Ilan arrives bearing letters in the handwriting of her brother Tomas — officially dead for two years — she learns the armistice she's been sent to deliver was forged to hand the republic to its executioners. To expose the forgery, Jude must carry the original documents past three military checkpoints, each guarded by men who once knew her face. She delivers the evidence to the neutral delegation at the eleventh hour; the signing stalls, and though the republic still falls, the record of the betrayal survives — as does she, finally visible.
about_author: Gideon Vasquez is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing the private papers of failed states. He writes historical fiction about the people history forgets to name — the couriers, clerks, and witnesses who carried its weight.

chapters.title: The Weight of Sealed Things
chapters.summary: In Jude's POV, we open on the last days of the Republic of Vessany: she is summoned to carry final diplomatic dispatches to the armistice city of Corvenne. Flashbacks establish her creed of invisibility and her grief over Tomas's death. The emotional beat is wary duty — she accepts the mission believing it is simply one more delivery.

chapters.title: Handwriting of the Drowned
chapters.summary: Still Jude's POV: at a river inn before the first checkpoint, a scarred stranger named Ilan corners her with letters unmistakably in Tomas's hand — dated after his death. He claims Tomas discovered the armistice terms were forged by General Marrec's faction. Torn between disbelief and hope, Jude compares the handwriting against her own memory. The beat is vertigo: her safe, invisible world cracks open.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints
chapters.summary: Alternating between Jude's tense crossings and brief interludes from the checkpoint officers who half-recognize her, this chapter drives the smuggling sequence: a bribe gone wrong at the bridge, a strip-search averted by a forged pass, and Ilan wounded covering her escape at the third gate. The climax arrives when she realizes the forged armistice is already being signed in Corvenne tonight. The beat is desperate momentum.

chapters.title: What Survives the Signing
chapters.summary: Jude's POV: she reaches the neutral delegation as pens hover over parchment and forces the original orders into the record, exposing Marrec's forgery. The republic cannot be saved, but the betrayal enters history under her name — the first time she signs anything. In the aftermath, she buries Tomas's letters beside the river and walks north with Ilan. The beat is costly, quiet vindication.
